rv.q: Outshining their material, we’re left with a feeling that, like Bonnie and Clyde themselves, the show could have been so much more, and should have done so much less.
The show, on the other hand, doesn’t linger long in the mind.
Regardless of these book-related quibbles, this is an excellent production firing on all cylinders.
This is a production that does much to restore the show’s reputation.

But for most of an overlong evening, the songs merely reiterate things we already know, not so much advancing the action as restating the obvious via one too many power ballads that may come across better out of context where they don’t slow down proceedings yet further.
Bonnie and Clyde is a showcase for Gage in particular, who has moved on smoothly from Romeo down the road in & Juliet, and boasts an intriguing interpretation of the ambitious Bonnie from McCann.
This is a musical that audiences will remember for a fantastic score and sensational performances.
As for this show dire is not the word. Atrocious is.

cn.t: This cult musical about Depression-era outlaws receives mixed reviews, with critics divided on its relentless energy. Strong performances, particularly from the female lead, elevate a show that struggles with its romanticization of killers.
